draft.title: Synaptic plasticity
card: Synaptic plasticity is the ability of synapses to change with experience. The brain keeps reshaping its connections through life.
a lasting strengthening of a synapse that is used often. Signals then pass across it more easily.
a lasting weakening of a synapse that is used rarely. Signals then pass across it less easily.
Other changes also reshape connections. Sprouting grows new branches to form new synapses. Rerouting forms a new path around damage. Pruning removes synapses that are rarely used.
draft.remember: Use strengthens a synapse and disuse weakens it, and the brain also grows, reroutes and prunes connections.

a.q: Jai practises a piano piece every day, and the synapses linking the neurons involved pass signals more easily over several weeks. What process does this show?
a.why: Frequent use has strengthened the connection so signals cross it more easily, which is long-term potentiation. Long-term depression is the opposite, a weakening of a connection that is rarely used.
a.clue: Is the connection being used more or less often?

b.q: After a stroke damages one area of Priya's brain, her neurons form a new pathway around the damage so she can regain some movement. Which process is this?
b.why: Rerouting is the formation of a new path around damaged neurons. Long-term potentiation is tempting because practice may strengthen the new path, but it describes a stronger synapse from frequent use, not the creation of a path around damage.
b.clue: Which process forms a path around damage rather than changing the strength of a synapse?

check.summary: No problems found. The card matches the VCE Study Design account of long-term potentiation, long-term depression, sprouting, rerouting and pruning, and both questions have one clear answer.
